apparatus.basis: Standard Greek loanword ⲕⲉⲫⲁⲗⲁⲓⲟⲛ 'Chapter'; central syllable damaged.
ⲉⲧ[ⲁⲛ]ϩ = ⲉⲧⲁⲛϩ̄ qualitative 'living' (Lyc. for ⲉⲧⲟⲛϩ̄), the standard descriptor of ⲥⲁⲣⲝ̄ in Manichaean cosmology — the living flesh inhabited by the soul.

Continuation of ⲁⲓⲧⲥⲉ-|-ⲃⲁⲕ 'I have taught you' from previous line; the 2sg.m suffix completes the verb.

notes.decision: Coptic numeral with overbar = ⲣ(100) + ⲓ(10) + ⲝ(60) = 170. This is the chapter number of the new kephalaion beginning here. The token appears three times (line 7 standalone; line 9 doubled within the title text), functioning as decorative chapter-number brackets that visually mark the title boundaries. Rendered '(170)' in English to preserve the numerical content; the syntactic title text reads continuously as 'Concerning why some delay coming forth from the body, while others die in a sudden event.'

ⲱⲥⲕ 'tarry, delay' + ⲁⲉⲓ 'to come' (infinitive of ⲉⲓ): 'delay to come' = 'delay coming.' Confirmed by recurrence in body text at lines 21-22 (ϣⲁⲩⲱⲥⲕ 'they delay habitually'; ⲛⲥⲉⲱⲥⲕ ⲁⲉⲓ 'and they delay coming') — the structuring verb of the kephalaion's question about manner of death.

ϣⲡⲛ̄ϣⲱⲡⲉ = ϣⲡⲛ̄ ('suddenly') + ϣⲱⲡⲉ ('happen, become') = 'sudden event/happening.' Standard Coptic compound for 'suddenness, sudden moment.' The chapter-title contrast is between gradual death (delayed exit of soul) and sudden death.

Lexeme uncertain. Possible analyses: (a) ⲙⲁⲛ-ⲥⲁⲧⲡ̄ 'place of choice/election' (compound on ⲙⲁⲛ- 'place of' + ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'choose'), with Lyc. ⲍ for ⲛ — fits Manichaean cosmological vocabulary; (b) corrupt scribal form. Preserved untranslated pending parallels.

Lexeme uncertain. Most plausibly ⲁϯ-ϩⲟⲩⲏⲛⲓⲁ, where -ϩⲟⲩⲏⲛⲓⲁ may render Greek εὔνοια 'goodwill, attentive disposition' (with Lyc. ⲍ-onset and vowel adjustment), giving 'with attention/goodwill.' The construction with ⲥⲱⲧⲙ̄ ('hear') + adverbial complement supports an attentive-listening sense. Preserved untranslated pending parallel attestations.
ⲁϩⲍⲙⲉⲥⲧ = ⲁϥ-ϩⲙⲟⲟⲥ-(ⲧ) Lyc. perfect 3sg.m of ϩⲙⲟⲟⲥ 'sit' (with ⲍ for ϩ regular Lyc.) + ⲁⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ 'downward' (in glossary). Standard Coptic 'he sat down' — closes the previous chapter's narrative frame.

Qualitative of ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'release, loose' (in glossary): 'is loosed forth, is released.' Used here of the soul being released from the body — the Manichaean technical register for death as loosing. Preserves the horizontal/dissolving semantics opposed to ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise.'

Lyc. ϩⲓⲣⲁⲧⲟⲩ 'at their foot' (cf. accumulated ⲍⲓⲣⲉⲧϩ̄ 'at the foot of'). In context — souls 'delaying to come at their foot' — the spatial-soteriological idiom describes failure to arrive into the proper supervisory presence/territory.
Lyc. = ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ 'he said' (in glossary). Standard Kephalaia narrative-frame opener for the apostle's response, following the disciples' double petition (lines 11-12 and 23-24).
